solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not long ago, left-winger moved to the middle again

parts.note: something that happened not long ago is recent
a Red is a socialist or communist, someone on the political left

explanation.surface: A politician who was once on the left has lately drifted back to the centre ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To recentre something is to put it back at the centre, so the past form means shifted to the middle once more.

clue.text: Flush and terribly sorry, having lost heart

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the heart of a word is its central letter, which is dropped from sorry

parts.note: sorry as written; its letters also happen to run backwards across terribly sorry, a coincidence and not the setter's mechanism

explanation.surface: Someone blushes red and feels awful, all their courage gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' drops the middle R from SORRY to leave SORY, and 'terribly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A flush is a reddening of the face, and a rosy complexion has that pink glow.

clue.text: Beat in court, briefly causing outcry

indicators.note: the word for beat is placed inside the shortened word for court
briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: court as written, a place of law
to lam is an informal word for to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed during a court case provokes a public outcry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like the definition but supplies LAM, a British informal verb for thrash; 'briefly' cuts the last letter of court.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud, insistent public protest, which is what an outcry is.

clue.text: Fool knocking container over

indicators.note: knocking something over tips it upside down, which in a down clue turns the word backwards
over completes knocking over, so the word for container is turned around

parts.note: a tin is a metal container

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool sends a box tumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking over' turns TIN upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nit, short for nitwit, is an informal British word for a stupid person.

clue.text: Odd drips around a fast-flowing stream

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the single letter given by the word a
odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of drips are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange drops of water gather round a swift-running brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges DRIPS, and 'around' puts those letters around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapids are a section of a river where the water runs fast and rough over rocks.

clue.text: Utterly depressed, correct?

parts.note: someone depressed feels down
correct means right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is accurate to call them completely miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adverb means thoroughly or completely, as in downright rude.

clue.text: Modern music king appearing in South Africa

indicators.note: the letter for king is shown appearing inside the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A star of contemporary music turns up in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican popular genre from the twentieth century, a forerunner of reggae.

clue.text: Clean area with dense vegetation

definitions.meaning: land covered with low, thick bushes

explanation.surface: Tidy up a patch of thick undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for vigorous washing and a noun for brushland covered with stunted shrubs.

clue.text: Ascetic American hiding in a tree, dishevelled

indicators.note: the abbreviation for American is concealed inside the other letters
dishevelled means untidy, so the letters of tree are messed up

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An unkempt, self-denying American lurks up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishevelled' rearranges TREE into TERE before 'hiding in' slips the American inside after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere describes a severe, self-disciplined way of living, close in sense to ascetic.

clue.text: Like a new business celebrity meeting organised workers quietly

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
TU stands for trade union, a body of organised workers
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A famous person sits down with union members for a discreet talk about a new venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Start-up as an adjective describes a newly founded company, so it fits the phrase like a new business.

clue.text: Imperfections — bedding material must be sent back

indicators.note: sending a word back means reading it from right to left

parts.note: straw is used as bedding for animals

explanation.surface: Faulty animal bedding has to be returned to the supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: Warts are small growths on the skin, so figuratively blemishes or flaws, as in warts and all.

clue.text: Think about getting proficient, becoming hugely important

parts.note: to consider something is to think about it
proficient means able or capable

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on becoming skilled and so rising to great prominence.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerable means notable or of real consequence, worth taking into account.

clue.text: See land as focus of attention

parts.note: to spot something is to see it
to light on or alight is to land, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Catching sight of the shore becomes the thing everyone looks at.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotlight is public attention, from the stage lamp that picks out one performer.

clue.text: Wine provided in summer — lots

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Plenty of wine is laid on during the summer months.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red grape variety and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Decorum in dirty hovel, way above

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece above comes first in the answer

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
a sty is a pigsty, any filthy dwelling

explanation.surface: Seemly behaviour is expected even in a filthy shack, with a road running past higher up.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is propriety in dress and behaviour, which is what decorum means.

clue.text: Take no notice of Italian man heading off

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: signore is the Italian for a gentleman or man

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to the Italian as he walks away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the S from SIGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to disregard them and pay them no heed.

clue.text: Fragrant old Dorothy has managed to get hugged

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside, so the word for managed goes within the name

parts.note: Dot is a short form of the name Dorothy
to run something is to manage it, so managed is ran

explanation.surface: Sweet-smelling old Dorothy has finally got a cuddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Dot is a familiar short form of Dorothy; 'to get hugged' signals the container. Odorant is more often a noun, but it is also an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Odorant can be an adjective meaning giving off a smell, so having a scent.

clue.text: Prepare for war — notice a fleet prepared to attack our shores

definitions.text: fleet prepared to attack our shores

parts.note: to arm is to equip forces for war
an ad, advertisement, is a public notice

explanation.surface: A call to readiness: a hostile fleet is massing against Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada of 1588 was a naval force sent to invade England; the word means any war fleet.

clue.text: Make idle one react differently, slowing down

indicators.note: made differently means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Getting a lazy person to respond in a new way means making things go slower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges all twelve letters of IDLE ONE REACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceleration is a reduction in speed, the opposite of acceleration.

clue.text: Ringing sound in prison

definitions.meaning: a sharp ringing sound, like glasses touching

explanation.surface: A bell tolls inside the jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the light chime of metal or glass and, colloquially, a prison.

clue.text: More than one drink is bad, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells you the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: something that ails is unwell or troubled, so is bad

explanation.surface: Someone claims that drinking several pints is reported to be harmful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ales are beers, so several of one kind of drink.

clue.text: Smart trick

definitions.meaning: to smart is to feel a sharp pain
a confidence trick or police set-up

explanation.surface: A clever ruse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the sharp hurt of being stung and an elaborate swindle.

clue.text: Correspondence on the up?

parts.note: letters going up into the sky are those carried by aeroplane rather than ground transport

explanation.definitionFit: This is post flown by aircraft, so letters literally travelling high above.

clue.text: Strange bottom, bottom not to be seem!

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter, the one taken away here
not to be seen (the clue's slip prints seem) says the letter vanishes from view

parts.note: the rump is the backside or bottom

explanation.surface: An odd backside, and one that ought to stay out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seem' is the clue's slip for 'seen'. 'bottom not to be seen' drops the last letter P from RUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a dated British informal adjective meaning odd or peculiar.

clue.text: Wild beast's jaw

definitions.meaning: a large shaggy ox of Tibet
to jaw or to ... is to chatter at length

explanation.surface: The jawbone of a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Himalayan bovine and is also slang for talking idly, which jaw also means.

clue.text: You hope they won't be the thorns in your side!

definitions.text: You hope they won't be the thorns in your side!

parts.words: You hope they won't be the thorns in your side!
parts.note: a thorn in your side is a nuisance; playfully, the people on your side are fellow players you hope will not annoy you

explanation.definitionFit: These are colleagues in the same team, literally those in your side.
